amazon:amazon:10604229.description:
Amazon has committed more than $10 billion to Amazon Leo, a low Earth orbit satellite network designed to bring fast, affordable broadband to customers around the world. Production Operations is where that ambition becomes physical. Every Leo satellite weighs more than 1,000 pounds, contains roughly 4 million individual components, and is designed and built in-house on a 172,000 square foot custom production line in Kirkland, Washington, capable of producing up to five satellite a day. The team completed its 1,000th satellite in September 2026 (https://www.aboutamazon.com/stories/how-amazon-leo-builds-satellites), making Leo one of the largest and most advanced satellite production operations in the world.
From the factory, satellites move to a 100,000 square foot payload processing facility at Kennedy Space Center in Florida that can support three launch campaigns at once, and to launch operations in French Guiana. With more than 80 launches secured across four launch providers, Leo plans to double its launch rate to more than 20 missions in its second year. The organization spans eight sites today across multiple states and ground stations across multiple countries, with more investments coming through in the times ahead.
This role builds on Amazon's deep operations heritage and takes it to newer heights. You will partner with an organization that brings together aerospace, RF, supply chain and manufacturing experts, recruited from the leading space and defense companies, alongside a skilled hourly production and launch workforce building and launching satellite in clean rooms, across shifts, and on mission-critical launch campaigns. Few people leaders anywhere get to shape all of this at once: precision satellite manufacturing across multiple satellite generations, export-controlled and government production, and Amazon Leo's first employing entity outside the US.
The people decisions made in the next 18 months will shape this organization for the next decade. As the senior PXT leader for Production Operations, you will make them alongside the VP of Production Operations and the multiple Directors who lead satellite manufacturing, launch operations, supply chain, quality, ground gateways, global trade and compliance, enterprise technology, and Manufacturing Systems Engineering and New Product Introduction. You won't be inheriting a playbook. You'll be writing it.
What makes this role unique
• Two talent markets, one interwoven strategy. Build differentiated people programs for a highly technical corporate workforce competing in one of the most constrained talent markets in the world, and for a large, fast growing hourly manufacturing and launch workforce, under a single coherent people strategy.
• Organization design at a defining moment. Shape org design, leadership formation, and succession as the organization scales across multiple satellite generations, direct-to-device, and government production in parallel, with a leadership team forming

Anvil Capture Systems · Hybrid [Boston, Massachusetts or Quebec, Canada], with travel to field sites · Full-time

 

About Anvil

Anvil Capture Systems is a Somerville, MA-based startup commercializing novel carbon dioxide removal technology. Anvil's mineralization-based process is patented, and uniquely measurable, affordable, scalable, and safe, making Anvil a highly competitive entrant in the sector. Anvil is based at Greentown Labs, the largest climate tech incubator in the world, with operations in Québec, Canada.

 

The Role

Reporting directly to Anvil's co-founders, the Director of Engineering will lead Anvil's commercial pilot project installation in Québec, and will help to design and scale the bulk material handling and downstream processing technology at the core of Anvil's process. We are looking for someone with a clear track record of designing, building, and operating first-of-a-kind plants in the mineral processing space.

 

What You'll Do

 - Own process design from concept through detailed engineering: PFDs, P&IDs, mass and energy balances, and equipment specifications

 - Scale Anvil's process from lab and pilot to commercial — size equipment, define comminution, classification, separation, and conveyance circuits, identify scale-up risks early and solve them

 - Integrate front-end mineral processing with downstream refinement steps

 - Work with third-party laboratories on test work and translate results into design decisions

 - Manage EPCs, equipment vendors, and fabricators to deliver builds on time and on budget

 - Lead facility commissioning and startup as Anvil's on-site technical supervisor

 - Maintain process documentation, technical logs, and lessons learned

 

What We're Looking For

 - Degree in mechanical or chemical engineering; a mechanical engineering foundation combined with surface mining and mineral processing experience

 - 10+ years of process engineering experience in mineral processing — we're specifically looking for mining and minerals backgrounds, not oil & gas, chemicals, or other process industries

 - Hands-on experience building facilities: you have taken at least one mineral processing or bulk material handling plant (ideally with multiple metallurgical steps) through design, construction, and startup

 - Proven ability to design and scale a process, not just operate or optimize an existing one

 - Direct commissioning and startup experience on new plants

 - Comfort in a small, fast-moving startup environment; prior early-stage company experience is a strong plus

 - Ready for regular travel between Boston and time spent on field sites in Québec and elsewhere

 

Nice to Haves

 - Process modeling tools; CAD experience (SolidWorks, AutoCAD)

 - First-of-a-kind or novel process development experience

 - Experience designing for harsh or remote environments

 

Compensation

Competitive base salary + equity. Relocation support available.

Blackpoint Cyber is the leading provider of world-class cybersecurity threat hunting, detection and remediation technology. Founded by former National Security Agency (NSA) cyber operations experts who applied their learnings to bring national security-grade technology solutions to commercial customers around the world, Blackpoint Cyber is in hyper-growth mode,  fueled by a recent $190m series C round. 


Company Culture

At Blackpoint Cyber, we value high-quality execution, ownership, and strong morals. Our principles are never tested, and we are proud to always do right by our customers. We are an energetic and collaborative team that maintains a high-performance culture and enables growth by overcoming challenges in the modern cyber threat landscape. If you are a driven professional with a passion for learning and contributing at a high level, Blackpoint Cyber welcomes you.

Position Overview
You will lead the engineering organization that builds our core product: finding threats across customer environments and getting them to the SOC fast. Reports to the Head of Engineering.

Scope

 - SIEM and log analytics

 - Endpoint detection and response

 - Identity threat detection

 - A rapid-response team focused on emerging threats

 - Quality engineering and architecture for detection systems

Responsibilities

 - Own detection coverage and quality: fewer missed threats, fewer false positives, faster time to detect.

 - Build detection-as-code practices: versioned rules, test data, regression suites and safe rollout.

 - Treat the SOC as your primary customer, and turn their escalations into fixes and coverage improvements.

 - Partner with ML engineering to bring AI-assisted detection and triage into production safely.

 - Improve the quality and consistency of the data detections depend on, with platform partners.

 - Respond quickly to new attack techniques, with a clear process from threat research to shipped detection.

 - Lead distributed teams, including contractors, with clear ownership and quality standards.

 - Hire and develop engineers and leaders; grow team leads into managers.

Required

 - 10+ years in software engineering, 3+ leading multiple teams or managers.

 - Hands-on background in security engineering: SIEM, EDR/MDR, identity or cloud detection.

 - Experience running high-volume event pipelines where data loss is not acceptable.

 - Ability to work closely with SOC analysts and turn their needs into engineering priorities.

Preferred

 - Detection engineering experience: MITRE ATT&CK mapping, rule authoring, threat hunting.

 - Experience managing offshore or contractor teams.

 - MSP or MDR provider background.

Blackpoint Cyber welcomes and encourages applications from qualified individuals of all races, colors, religions, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, marital status, or any other legally protected status. We are committed to equality of opportunity in all aspects of employ

About Delinea:
Delinea is the identity security platform that continuously controls what AI agents, humans and machines can do and for how long. It extends privileged access management from the point of access to the moment of action, using just-in-time authorization to reduce standing privilege across on-premises, multi-cloud and short-lived infrastructure, without adding friction for legitimate users. Delinea provides visibility across every identity type, scores the risk each one carries, and preserves the context behind access decisions, making them auditable and defensible. It supports both static and ephemeral access, letting teams apply Zero Standing Privilege where risk demands it without replacing existing infrastructure.



About the role

Delinea is looking for a strategic, hands-on Director, People Business Partner to partner with our Product, Technology, and AI leaders. You'll be the main people advisor to the EVP of Product & Technology and the AI leader. You'll help shape how we organize, hire, develop, and keep the technical talent behind our identity security platform. This role sits on the Global PBP leadership team and helps set the people strategy for the whole company.

This is a pivotal moment to join. Product & Technology is moving to a General Manager (GM) model: the EVP of Product & Technology will lead three GMs, each owning a specialized vertical. You'll be a key partner in making this model work. You'll help leaders set decision rights, define how the GMs and shared functions work together, and adapt talent, org design, and performance practices to fit.

What you'll do

 - GM operating model design: Partner with the EVP of Product & Technology and the three General Managers to design and embed the GM operating model:

 - Define decision rights across the GMs, the EVP, and shared functions (who decides, who is consulted, who executes) so accountability is clear and decisions move faster.

 - Design how each GM business works with shared functions such as Engineering platform, Product Ops, Finance, and the People team, including interfaces, governance forums, and escalation paths.

 - Adapt org design, talent, and performance practices to the GM model: span-and-layer design, leadership roles and capability gaps, succession, goal setting, and how performance and rewards reflect GM-level accountability.

 - Lead the people side of the change, including sequencing, leader readiness, communications, and adoption metrics.

 - Enterprise people strategy: Use what the GM transformation teaches us to shape people programs and practices across Delinea:

 - Turn what works in P&T into repeatable principles, playbooks, and tools for decision rights, org design, and performance practices.

 - Partner with the Global PBP team and the People COEs (Talent, Total Rewards, People Ops) to adapt and scale these approaches to other functions where they fit.

 - Act as a thought partner to the VP, Global PBPs on enterprise org effectiveness,

ABOUT DOT.CARDS http://DOT.CARDS

dot.cards http://dot.cards is building the platform for what happens after people connect in the real world. We began by making it effortless to share a digital profile with a tap. With 2.5M+ devices sold and 100M+ in-person connections facilitated, we now have a rare foundation: consumer scale, real-world distribution, and direct insight into how people connect.

Our products bring together digital profiles, contact exchange, consumer subscriptions, business software, and physical devices in one connected experience. We are a revenue-backed company based in Los Angeles, with an opportunity to make those experiences more useful for individuals and teams. This role will shape the engineering organization and technical foundations behind that work.




THE ROLE

Reporting directly to our Founder & CEO, you will lead technical direction and the engineering organization at dot.cards http://dot.cards. You’ll partner as a peer with Product and Design, with meaningful influence over architecture, hiring, and how we turn ideas into products.

We're reimagining enterprise Identity and Access Management from the ground up. Founded by serial entrepreneurs Shai Morag and Tal Marom and backed by a $60M seed round from Greylock, Accel, and CRV, we're building the next generation of identity security. Identity is the gateway to everything- who's let in, who's kept out, and it's now the number one attack vector in the enterprise. The tools built to govern it were designed for a slower world of human users and static environments. That world is gone. Identities are exploding across human, machine, and AI agents faster than legacy systems can track, and security teams are left patching together five disconnected tools that still can't answer "who has access to what, right now." We think the answer isn't another point solution- it's a new foundation. Oak is the AI-native Identity Operating System: an AI connector framework that reaches any application, a live identity graph built from raw evidence, and a team of AI agents that governs the full lifecycle of every identity in one platform. ashby:quo:c6343e67-f8fa-4cbc-bdb6-9299e2.description:
Small businesses represent 99.9% of all companies, yet they're still forced to choose between clunky, outdated enterprise phone systems or their personal phones. This multi-billion dollar market has been overlooked for decades, left to cobble together solutions that slow them down instead of helping them grow.

 

Quo is changing that. We bring calls, texts, and customer information together into one easy-to-use, AI-powered platform. We're not just building a phone system. We're setting a new standard for how businesses connect with their customers.

 

Driven by our values, we move fast, build with determination, and obsess over delivering value to the businesses that have been underserved for far too long.

 

Today, Quo is trusted by more than 120,000 companies and rated #1 in customer satisfaction on G2. We're backed by Y Combinator, Tiger Global, Craft Ventures, Slow Ventures, and other top-tier investors. It's safe to say we're onto something big.


ABOUT THE ROLE



We're looking for a Director of Technical Support to build Tier 3 Technical Support from the ground up. Tier 3 will be our specialist support engineering function for the most complex customer issues across our AI products, Model Context Protocol (MCP) capabilities, APIs, integrations, and telecom infrastructure.



Tier 2 has built a strong foundation, and Tier 3 will build on it. You'll define the mandate, hire and grow the team, and establish clear ownership and handoffs across Support, Product, Engineering, and Engineering QA. You'll partner closely with Support leadership, who will continue to own Tier 1 and Tier 2 performance.



You'll build the team's ability to investigate complex issues, reproduce defects, deliver actionable technical escalations, and validate fixes with Engineering and QA. You'll set standards for technical judgment and customer ownership, with accountability for faster diagnosis, reliable resolution, and fewer recurring issues.



As we optimize support, you'll focus Tier 3 on the work where deeper technical expertise has the greatest impact. You'll partner with Engineering and CX Operations on tools, AI, and automation that improve resolution and reduce manual effort, while owning priorities, adoption, and measurable customer outcomes.



You'll also be the senior CX partner to Product and Engineering, turning customer challenges into shared priorities for better products, more reliable service, and stronger launch readiness.




SOME OF THE THINGS YOU’LL DO:



Design and launch Tier 3

 - Define Tier 3’s mandate: Establish the operating model and escalation criteria, with clear ownership boundaries across Tier 2, Product, and Engineering.

 - Build the technical foundation: Define the capabilities needed to resolve complex issues across APIs, integrations, MCP, telecom, and AI products.

 - Create a phased roadmap: Plan team structure, specialist roles, tooling, access, and email and phone support.

 - Prioritize investments: Make clear tradeoffs

Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai https://shield.ai/. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/shield-ai, X https://x.com/shieldaitech, Instagram https://www.instagram.com/shield_ai, and YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@Shield_AI. 

 


JOB DESCRIPTION:

The Head of Product Design will define and lead the user experience vision for Hivemind, Shield AI’s autonomy development platform. This role is responsible for transforming complex autonomy, robotics, AI, and developer workflows into intuitive experiences that enable engineers, operators, and organizations to develop and deploy resilient autonomy at scale. 

A major focus of this role will be shaping the next generation of AI-native and agent-driven workflows across the autonomy lifecycle. As Hivemind evolves from traditional software tooling toward AI-assisted autonomy development, simulation, evaluation, deployment, and operations, this leader will help invent entirely new ways for users to collaborate with AI systems, agents, and foundation-model-powered tools. The ideal candidate has deep experience designing AI products, developer platforms, or complex technical systems and can translate emerging AI capabilities into workflows that dramatically improve user productivity and outcomes. 

This is a highly hands-on role as this leader will manage a team of elite designers. During the first 6–12 months, most of the time will be spent conducting user research, designing experiences, prototyping concepts, facilitating product discovery, and partnering directly with Product and Engineering teams to define the future of autonomy development. 

What you'll do:

 - 


USER RESEARCH & PRODUCT DISCOVERY 

 - Lead customer research efforts across product development, customer engagement, and solutions teams to identify pain points, workflows, unmet needs, and product opportunities. 

 - Establish scalable mechanisms for gathering, synthesizing, and communicating user insights throughout the product development lifecycle. 

 - Translate customer and operational feedback into actionable product recommendations, requirements, and design initiatives. 


PRODUCT DESIGN & USER EXPERIENCE 

 - Design end-to-end workflows across autonomy development, simulation, testing, analysis, deployment, and operations. 

 - Create intuitive experiences for highly technical users including autonomy engineers, software developers, operators, and mission planners. 

 - Simplify complex system architectures, data flows, infrastructure tooling, and AI workflows into understandable us

We are seeking a Director of Systems Engineering & Architecture (SE&A) for Shield AI’s Hivemind Enterprise organization, supporting development of our autonomy platform and development ecosystem for AI Pilots. This leader will oversee Systems Engineering, System Architecture, Cybersecurity Engineering, and Safety/Airworthiness Engineering, building the teams and technical practices needed to deliver dependable, software-intensive autonomous systems.

 

You will connect operational product needs to measurable requirements, coherent architectures, and credible verification and assurance evidence. Partnering with Product, Software Engineering, Program Management, and Integration and Test teams, you will embed practical engineering rigor throughout the development lifecycle.

What You'll Do:

 - 

 - Lead the team: Hire, develop, and lead the SE&A engineering disciplines, establishing clear responsibilities, technical standards, and effective cross-functional partnerships.

 - Establish the operating model: Define how SE&A engages with product and engineering teams, prioritizes competing demands, and allocates resources. Establish clear decision rights, escalation paths, and risk-proportionate engineering practices that improve delivery without unnecessary process overhead.

 - Own requirements and architecture: Guide requirements development and management, system modeling, architectural trade studies, interface definition, traceability, and change impact analysis.

 - Drive verification and validation planning: Establish system-level verification and validation strategies, measurable acceptance criteria, and evidence expectations. Partner with integration and test teams to demonstrate end-to-end capability.

 - Support software development: Integrate systems engineering and architecture into iterative planning, design, implementation, testing, release readiness, and sustainment.

 - Lead integrated assurance: Ensure cybersecurity, safety, and airworthiness considerations shape requirements, architecture, development, and verification from the outset.

 - Guide technical decisions: Lead risk-based design reviews, resolve cross-team technical issues, and provide evidence-based readiness recommendations while preserving designated approval and risk-acceptance authorities.

About the role:

We're hiring a hands-on Director of Enterprise Security to lead Security Engineering, the Security Operations Center (SOC), and Identity & Access Management (IAM). You'll own security across the whole enterprise: end-user computing, applications, data, SaaS, cloud, international sites and manufacturing. You'll set technical direction, build strong teams and turn strategy into measurable results in a fast-moving defense-technology environment.


Key Responsibilities:

 - Lead and grow the Security Engineering, SOC and IAM teams. Hire, mentor and build a high-performing culture.

 - Provide hands-on technical leadership on architecture, tooling and engineering decisions. Act as the senior technical authority for enterprise security.

 - Own security architecture and controls for endpoints, applications, data, SaaS, cloud, international locations and manufacturing/OT environments.

 - Run 24x7 detection, response and threat-hunting capabilities, and mature incident response playbooks and metrics.

 - Drive the IAM strategy, including identity lifecycle, SSO/MFA, privileged access and zero-trust principles.

 - Align security programs with defense compliance requirements (NIST SP 800-171, CMMC, DFARS, ITAR/EAR) in partnership with GRC, IT and Legal.

 - Set the roadmap, budget and KPIs, and report risk and program progress to executive leadership.

 - Work with Engineering, IT, Manufacturing and Business teams to make security effective while still enabling the business.

Historically, US Healthcare has relied on a fee-for-service reimbursement system where providers are paid based on the quantity of patient visits and procedures, rather than the quality of health outcomes.

At Stellar Health, we help primary care providers put patient health first. Our platform - a mix of technology, people, and analytics - supports providers at the point of care, delivering real-time patient information, activating practice staff, and empowering providers and care teams with incentives that reward the work they are already doing to keep patients healthy. Using the Stellar App, our web-based, point-of-care tool; practices receive a simple checklist of recommended actions that support the best quality care. Providers and care teams are then paid monthly for each action they complete, and Payors save money in reduced healthcare costs along the way.

OUR MISSION

We exist to create a more connected, compassionate, and confident experience for people with cancer and those who care for them. We make it easier to get answers, access high-quality care quickly, and feel supported throughout treatment and beyond.

Today, Thyme Care is a market-leading value-based oncology care enabler, partnering with national and regional health plans, providers, and employers to deliver better outcomes and lower costs for thousands of people across the country. Our model combines high-touch human support with powerful technology and AI to bring together everyone involved in a person's cancer journey: caregivers, oncologists, health plans, and employers.

Data is the backbone of that model. It is how we identify the right members and bring them into care, how we measure whether we are improving outcomes and cost, how we reconcile and build trust with our partners, and increasingly how AI gives our care team time back to spend with people. When our data is accurate, timely, and trusted, everyone from a nurse mid-call to a health plan executive can act with confidence.

If you're inspired to make cancer care more human and to help reimagine what's possible, we'd love to meet you. Together, we can build a future where every person with cancer feels truly cared for, in every moment that matters.

RFA is a leading IT and cybersecurity partner to financial services firms: hedge funds, private equity, asset managers, and the firms that serve them. RFA is part of Titan, which is building the AI workforce for IT.

Titan has raised over $100M from General Catalyst, 8VC, and CalPERS, acquired market-leading IT firms like RFA, and put AI agents into production in large enterprises. We've automated 100K+ tickets across 800+ customers and are leading the industry in service quality. Our tech team has talent from Scale AI, CoreWeave, Vanta, Dropbox, Meta, FiveRings, TwoSigma, Amazon, Harvard, Stanford, and MIT.

Why this role, why now

Attackers targeting financial firms have moved to identity: MFA fatigue, session token theft, mailbox takeover. Catching that across 100+ client environments takes well-built detections, clean telemetry and fast automation. More analysts won't solve it.

We're looking for a builder who also leads. You'll design and run the stack behind RFA's SOC, put Titan's AI agents to work on triage and response, and lead the team that handles what the agents can't.

About the role

As Director of Security Operations & Detection Engineering, you own RFA's detection and response capability end to end. That covers the SIEM, EDR and identity telemetry, the detections and playbooks, how every new client gets onboarded, and the analysts who run it 24/7. You'll report to RFA's CISO. You'll also work closely with Titan's engineering team, who build the agents and automation from your requirements.

You'll measure success by time to detect and contain, detection coverage across client environments, false-positive and escalation rates, and incidents caught before they become client problems.

This role is remote (US).

Videa is the most adopted dental AI platform, used by 90,000 clinicians. Our vision is to be the first company to diagnose a billion people.

**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

Amazon has committed more than $10 billion to Amazon Leo, a low Earth orbit satellite network designed to bring fast, affordable broadband to customers around the world. Production Operations is where that ambition becomes physical. Every Leo satellite weighs more than 1,000 pounds, contains roughly 4 million individual components, and is designed and built in-house on a 172,000 square foot custom production line in Kirkland, Washington, capable of producing up to five satellite a day. The team completed its 1,000th satellite in September 2026 (https://www.aboutamazon.com/stories/how-amazon-leo-builds-satellites), making Leo one of the largest and most advanced satellite production operations in the world.  
From the factory, satellites move to a 100,000 square foot payload processing facility at Kennedy Space Center in Florida that can support three launch campaigns at once, and to launch operations in French Guiana. With more than 80 launches secured across four launch providers, Leo plans to double its launch rate to more than 20 missions in its second year. The organization spans eight sites today across multiple states and ground stations across multiple countries, with more investments coming through in the times ahead.  
This role builds on Amazon's deep operations heritage and takes it to newer heights. You will partner with an organization that brings together aerospace, RF, supply chain and manufacturing experts, recruited from the leading space and defense companies, alongside a skilled hourly production and launch workforce building and launching satellite in clean rooms, across shifts, and on mission-critical launch campaigns. Few people leaders anywhere get to shape all of this at once: precision satellite manufacturing across multiple satellite generations, export-controlled and government production, and Amazon Leo's first employing entity outside the US.  
The people decisions made in the next 18 months will shape this organization for the next decade. As the senior PXT leader for Production Operations, you will make them alongside the VP of Production Operations and the multiple Directors who lead satellite manufacturing, launch operations, supply chain, quality, ground gateways, global trade and compliance, enterprise technology, and Manufacturing Systems Engineering and New Product Introduction. You won't be inheriting a playbook. You'll be writing it.  
What makes this role unique  

* Two talent markets, one interwoven strategy. Build differentiated people programs for a highly technical corporate workforce competing in one of the most constrained talent markets in the world, and for a large, fast growing hourly manufacturing and launch workforce, under a single coherent people strategy.
* Organization design at a defining moment. Shape org design, leadership formation, and succession as the organization scales across multiple satellite generations, direct-to-device, and government production

-------------------------------------------

Location: Spartanburg, SC (on site, five days a week)

The Senior Director, Information Technology leads one or more technology teams at ACA and is an emerging leader in our succession bench. This is a role for a strong, hands-on technologist who is ready to take on broader leadership and wants to grow toward executive responsibility with active coaching from senior IT leadership and the CIO.

board-indeed:anduril:in-71b26621a8ed3604.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century's most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril's family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

**ABOUT THE TEAM**  
  
The duty of this organization is to enable our Customers' ongoing Mission Readiness. From the moment they say "go" until the contract is fulfilled. We are only successful when the customer's mission is successful.  
  
Mission Readiness is the post-production shared services organization for Anduril. This team supports the Business Lines and Divisions throughout the lifecycle of their product, from initial sustainment concept through delivery, installation, operation, repair and return. These service offerings also include providing technical publications, training, customer support, connectivity services and other value-added services. To the degree the Business elects, we accept the delegated responsibility for upfront and continued delivery of the committed service solutions. This team endeavors to provide the Business Lines, as our internal customers, shared mission services that are more efficient and cost effective than if they chose to provide them directly. By offering mission support capabilities and capacity that are not "core" to the Business, the Business can focus resources on addressing the next big need while we ensure existing commitments are met.  
  
Within Mission Readiness, our Maintenance Repair & Overhaul (MRO) function provides capability to repair durable products to extend their useful life.  
Repair Engineering is the core technical function for Anduril's component and hardware in-house maintenance capabilities.  
  
**ABOUT THE JOB**  
  
We are looking for a Director of Repair Engineering to build, from the ground up, the technical engineering backbone of Anduril's repair function. This discipline is nascent at Anduril today. Production engineers handle returns, but the dedicated practice of assessing acceptable wear, developing non-production repair methods, and determining when a product is 'serviceable but not like new' does not yet exist as a standalone function. You will create it. Where our Head of MRO is building and running the repair organization itself, this role owns the engineering rigor underneath it: the repair-versus-discard decisions, the maintenance task analyses, the repair procedures and the product support data that determine what gets fixed, how, and at what level
board-indeed:anduril:in-71b26621a8ed3604.title: Director of Repair Engineering

**Aspire Public Schools NorCal — Senior Director, AI, Data & Systems Engineering**

**Job Description**

**About Aspire NorCal**

Founded in 1998, Aspire Public Schools has served scholars and communities across California for nearly three decades. With Aspire Los Angeles transitioning into an independent organization, the Bay Area and Central Valley regions are coming together to form Aspire NorCal, operating 22 schools serving approximately 10,000 scholars across Northern California (Oakland, Richmond, East Palo Alto, Sacramento, Stockton, Modesto, and Ceres).

This evolution comes at an important moment for Aspire. Changes in California’s funding, policy, enrollment, and operating environment have created an opportunity to rethink how the organization supports its schools and scholars in its next chapter. The formation of Aspire NorCal creates an opportunity to strengthen support for schools across teams previously organized by geography, improve the consistency and effectiveness of school support, and create clear accountability systems for organizational and scholar outcomes. The new model will require the organization to balance greater coherence across Aspire NorCal with responsiveness to the different communities and contexts of its schools.

Aspire NorCal enters this transition with a long-standing mission focused on post-secondary success and a deep commitment to educational equity, along with decades of institutional knowledge across its schools and teams. Preserving those strengths while building Aspire NorCal as a unified region will be central to the work ahead.

We use AI to get there, and we set the policy and training that keep it useful and appropriately safe. The team is made up of an Enablement team that builds the shared foundation, plus pods that each serve a customer group: School Operations & Principals, Academics & Teachers, and People & Resources. Our working principles: go deep with users, one shared foundation, self-serve first, learning is the job, and nobody works alone.

We are seeking a seasoned, hands-on **Interim Chief Information Security Officer** to lead its enterprise information security program for a 3–6 month engagement. The Interim CISO will provide immediate executive leadership, stabilize and assess the security program, protect patient data and clinical operations, maintain regulatory compliance, and position the organization for a smooth handoff to a permanent CISO.

The ideal candidate is a proven security executive who has led security programs inside hospitals or health systems, understands the realities of protecting clinical environments where uptime directly affects patient care, and can earn credibility quickly with executives, clinicians, IT teams and the board.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Leadership & Program Stewardship**

* Serve as the organization's senior information security executive, owning the cybersecurity strategy, program and team for the duration of the engagement.
* Within the first 30 days, assess the current security posture, team, tooling, open risks and in-flight initiatives, and deliver a prioritized 90-day action plan.
* Lead, mentor and stabilize the information security team; identify staffing and skill gaps.
* Brief executive leadership, the Board of Trustees and relevant committees on cyber risk, program status and incidents in clear, business-focused language.
* Manage security budget, vendors and managed-service partners.

**Risk, Compliance & Governance**

**Cascades Healthcare, Provo Utah**

Cascades Healthcare is seeking an experienced, hands-on Director of Information Technology to lead and oversee technology operations supporting our skilled nursing facilities and corporate offices.

The IT Director is responsible for ensuring the security, reliability, efficiency, and effectiveness of the organization's technology infrastructure, systems, and support services. This position provides leadership and direction to the IT support team while working collaboratively with facility administrators, department leaders, and corporate leadership to support daily operations and quality resident care.

The ideal candidate is a proactive, solutions-oriented leader who combines strong technical expertise with effective team management, communication, and problem-solving skills. This individual must be comfortable managing multiple priorities, resolving complex technical challenges, and implementing technology solutions across multiple healthcare locations.

**Duties and Responsibilities**

* **IT Leadership and Operations:** Lead, supervise, and develop the IT support team while overseeing technology operations across multiple facilities. Manage networks, servers, equipment, and business applications, ensuring timely technical support, effective troubleshooting, and reliable systems that support daily operations.
* **Cybersecurity, Compliance, and Systems Management:** Oversee cybersecurity, HIPAA compliance, data protection, system access, backups, and disaster recovery. Collaborate with HR and facility leadership to manage employee access, maintain technology inventories, and ensure secure and efficient systems.
* **Strategic Planning, Budgeting, and Facility Support:** Manage IT vendors, contracts, purchasing, budgets, and technology projects, including system upgrades and new facility integrations. Communicate with executive leadership, identify cost-saving opportunities, travel to facilities as needed, and coordinate responses to urgent technology issues.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent education, experience, and certifications, with a minimum of five years of progressive IT experience, including leadership or supervisory responsibilities.
* Strong technical expertise in multi-location IT infrastructure, networking, servers, Microsoft 365, Windows systems, cloud applications, cybersecurity, and technical troubleshooting.
* Proven ability to lead and develop teams, manage IT projects, vendors, and budgets, communicate effectively, and maintain confidentiality of sensitive information.
* Ability to work on-site in the Provo/Orem, Utah area, travel to company facilities, and respond to urgent technology needs as required.

At CivicPlus, we strive to bring our company vision to life through innovation and collaboration. Supported by approachable leadership and transparent communication, we're empowered to make an impact on local government and the residents they serve. Grow your career alongside great people, where authenticity is welcome, successes are celebrated, and potential is nurtured.

**Your Impact**  
The Director of Governance, Risk & Compliance builds and owns CivicPlus's information security compliance and risk management programs. This hire will design, formalize, and run both programs end to end so they hold up in audits, scale across products, and earn trust with public sector customers.

As a Director of Governance, Risk & Compliance, you will:

#### **Make a Difference Where It Matters Most**

Join a team that’s been providing compassionate, patient-centered care to rural North Carolina communities for 50 years. At CommWell Health, you won’t just care for patients, you’ll empower families, change lives, and be part of a mission-driven team that believes everyone deserves quality healthcare, close to home.

  

#### **What You’ll Do**

The Director of Information Technology is responsible for the leadership, planning, implementation, security, and daily operation of CommWell Health's technology environment. This position provides oversight of infrastructure, cybersecurity, telecommunications, end-user support, cloud services, technology vendors, disaster recovery, business continuity, technology budgeting, asset management, and IT service delivery.

The Director serves as the primary technology liaison between CommWell Health and Health Choice Network (HCN), managed service providers, cybersecurity consultants, telecommunications providers, software vendors, and technology partners. The Director is responsible for establishing operational priorities, maintaining a secure technology environment, ensuring accountability of Information Technology personnel, and supporting organizational objectives through the effective use of technology resources.

Collaborates with Facilities, Operations, Clinical Leadership, architects, engineers, contractors, telecommunications providers, and technology vendors during new construction, renovation, and expansion projects. Responsible for planning, budgeting, coordinating, and overseeing technology infrastructure requirements including structured cabling, network architecture, wireless connectivity, telecommunications, security systems, audiovisual systems, access control, surveillance systems, internet services, equipment deployment, and technology readiness for occupancy.

This position reports directly to the CIO/CVO and serves as a strategic leader supporting CommWell Health's mission, operational goals, regulatory compliance requirements, and long-term technology strategy.

  

#### **What We’re Looking For**

**Required:**

* Bachelor's Degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Healthcare Information Technology, Business Administration, or related field.

  

* Minimum seven (7) years of progressive Information Technology leadership experience.
* Minimum three (3) years of direct supervisory experience managing technical personnel.
* Experience leading technology infrastructure, cybersecurity, networking, telecommunications, and support operations.
* Experience managing technology budgets and vendor relationships.
* Experience developing and implementing technology policies, procedures, and operational standards.
* Experience leading complex technology projects and organizational technology initiative
* Valid North Carolina Driver's License

**Preferred:**

* Master's Degree in Information Technology, Health Informatics

board-indeed:compass international holdi.description:
At Compass, our mission is to help everyone find their place in the world. Founded in 2012, we’re revolutionizing the real estate industry with our end-to-end platform that empowers residential real estate agents to deliver exceptional service to seller and buyer clients.

**About the Role:**

The Director of the Security Operations Center owns detection, response, and threat hunting across our production, corporate, and cloud environments. This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You will set the direction of the SOC in line with the CISO's security strategy and run a team of senior technical professionals day to day. When an incident calls for it, you will step in personally and lead the investigation and response. You report directly to the CISO and act as their operational partner, so the CISO always has an accurate picture of threats, exposure, and our ability to respond.

**What you will do:**

* Turn the CISO's security strategy into a SOC roadmap, prioritize where detection and response investment goes, and show measurable progress against it.
* Own the end-to-end detection and response lifecycle, from telemetry collection through detection, triage, containment, eradication, recovery, and corrective action.
* Act as incident commander for the highest-severity events. Get hands-on in the investigation, analyze logs, endpoint, network, identity, and cloud telemetry yourself, and make containment decisions under pressure.
* Build, lead, and develop a team of incident response, detection, and threat hunting engineers. Set a high technical bar, coach people through hard investigations, and hold the team accountable for quality and follow-through.
* Hold your ground on technical and risk decisions with engineering, product, IT, and executive stakeholders. Push back with evidence when a decision increases exposure, and escalate clearly when needed.
* Design and evolve the SOC architecture, including SIEM, SOAR, EDR, identity, and cloud detection tooling. Decide what to build, what to buy, and what to retire.
* Drive an automation-first operating model that cuts manual triage, shortens time to detect and contain, and lets the team scale without adding headcount in step with the environment.
* Establish full telemetry coverage across the Compass platform, including acquired environments, so that every critical asset produces attributable, correlated events.
* Lead a threat-informed defense program. Use adversary behavior, threat intelligence, and hunting results to drive detection engineering and active defense capabilities.
* Own the incident response plan, severity definitions, escalation paths, and on-call model. Run realistic tabletop and live-fire exercises that include technical teams and executives.
* Run blameless post-incident reviews and make sure corrective actions have an identified owner, a deadline, and verified completion.
* Define and report the operational metrics that matter, such as coverage, detection fidelity, dwell time,

DawnSecurity is building a next-generation cybersecurity platform. At its core is a hard applied-research problem, and this role owns it: leading our Data Science and Data Engineering team, directing algorithm research, building the models behind the platform, and driving the company's intellectual property.

### **What makes this role different**

This is not a "train a classifier on labeled data" role. The core challenges are:

* Learning without labels. The events that matter most are too rare to train on. Models must be built from structure, statistics, and synthetically generated signal rather than labeled examples.
* Probabilistic modeling over graphs. The problem domain is inherently relational — entities, hierarchies, and connections — and the models must reason over that structure, not just over flat feature vectors.
* Adversarially robust learning. An adversary can influence the data our models learn from. Robustness to manipulation and governed model updates are first-class design constraints.
* Explainability as a requirement. Every score must decompose into a sentence a domain expert can act on. Opaque models that outperform explainable ones by a margin still lose here.
* LLMs as components, not oracles. We use LLMs inside pipelines with statistical quality gates and human-in-the-loop escalation — knowing when not to trust model output is the skill.

### **Core Responsibilities**

### **Research & Modeling Leadership**

* Own the research agenda: from hypothesis through prototype, empirical validation, shadow-mode deployment, and production.
* Design probabilistic and statistical models for sparse, high-cardinality event data — scoring, smoothing, calibration, drift detection.
* Lead graph-based modeling: entity resolution across heterogeneous sources, inference over large graphs, relationship discovery with tiered confidence.
* Combine statistical models with rule- and constraint-based reasoning where the two must agree.
* Define the evaluation discipline: synthetic data, shadow-mode comparisons, calibration audits, and precision targets tied to user trust.

### **IP Creation & Protection**

* Drive patentable inventions from the research roadmap: identify novel mechanisms, validate them empirically, and work with patent counsel on claims.
* Distinguish what to file, what to publish, and what to keep as trade secret — and sequence research disclosures accordingly.

* Balance startup velocity against platform sustainability; keep compute costs proportionate to value.

------------

Fanatics is a leading global sports platform redefining how fans connect with the teams, players and moments they love. **About the Organization**
--------------------------

Millions of Americans feel politically homeless and left out of the two-party structure. Too many electoral choices are settled before most voters have a meaningful say, and our political system consistently fails to address the nation’s biggest challenges. We are a stealth team building an ambitious cross-partisan political venture to make American democracy more open, competitive, and responsive. We will build the infrastructure to effectively challenge the two-party political establishment, and create fundamentally new pathways to elected office and engaged citizen participation.

Our first major initiative will launch publicly in spring 2027 with the objective of materially influencing the 2028 national election cycle. This project will combine the scale of a mainstream consumer technology product, the reach of a modern media operation, and the ground game of a national political campaign – complete with digital and IRL field organizing across dozens of states – to engage tens of millions of Americans and build a constituency that outlasts this election cycle.

Our leadership team has raised and deployed over $100M toward democracy reform, winning dozens of state and local reform campaigns. Backed by seed funding from prominent investors and a cross-partisan board of civic leaders and company-builders, we are now assembling a multidisciplinary operating team of technologists, storytellers, politicos, and operators to build it from the ground up.

**About the Role**
------------------

You are a technologist who believes in the American political experiment and is convinced that more political competition is needed for a more productive, representative government. As our *Chief Technology Officer,* you will architect and build a civic consumer product with a fixed launch date that millions of Americans will join to inform themselves, deliberate together, and make their voices count in 2028. You will own every engineering decision, including how you build the team and choose partner firms. You are comfortable doing this under a media microscope, with adversaries actively seeking any crack in security to show that the system can't be trusted. In short, you'll build a secure, leading-edge platform that brings our democracy into the 21st century.

About the Role:

Lead the operating system for Technology Operations. This role brings together service management, operational command, reliability enablement, performance assurance, Test Data Management, FinOps, governance, readiness, operational intelligence, and automation to create transparent accountability and sustained improvement across technology services.

The role owns enterprise standards, shared enablement capabilities, independent visibility, facilitation, measurement, and escalation. It does not assume engineering accountability for the services it evaluates. Application, product, infrastructure, and platform owners remain responsible for remediation, SLO attainment, recovery, security, quality, performance, and cost within the services they own.

**Leadership model**
====================

The organization is delivered through four primary functions:

* IT Service Management (ITSM)
* Network Operations Center (NOC)
* Financial Operations (FinOps)
* Technology Operations Governance (OpsGov)

**Core responsibilities**
=========================

**Service Management & Operations**
-----------------------------------

* Own the enterprise ITSM operating model and operate ServiceNow as an enterprise product with accountable product ownership, roadmap, engineering capacity, adoption measures, service experience, and measurable value realization.
* Govern and continuously improve incident, major incident, change, problem, request, knowledge, service catalog, configuration, CMDB, service mapping, SLA/OLA, and continual-service-improvement practices.
* Establish measurable service levels and adoption outcomes for ITSM capabilities, including process compliance, user experience, workflow cycle time, self-service adoption, knowledge effectiveness, CMDB quality, service ownership, and realized value from the enterprise service-management platform.
* Lead the NOC as a global operational command capability for monitoring, event triage, escalation, communications, runbook execution, and selected repeatable operational activities.

**A Day in the Life:**

The Director of IT Service Management leads the design, delivery, and continuous improvement of Hertz’s global IT service management practices. This role turns technology and business priorities into reliable, measurable service operations, supporting a consistent experience for employees and business partners across the company.

Working with Technology and business leaders, the Director oversees key service management processes and the systems that support them, including ServiceNow. The role partners closely with infrastructure, end-user services, application, cybersecurity, and operations teams to improve service quality, system stability, resiliency, and compliance. It also manages team performance, budgets, and vendor relationships within the scope of responsibility, using operational data and service metrics to guide decisions and improvements.

* Oversee the ServiceNow platform roadmap and backlog, partnering with stakeholders on enhancements, automation, integrations, and adoption.

* Manage the service management budget and assigned resources, balancing service needs, risk, and cost.
* Set expectations for vendors and service providers supporting ITSM processes; monitor service levels, delivery, governance, and cost-effectiveness.
* Ensure service management policies and procedures reflect current practices and support compliance with applicable requirements, including SOX, PCI, IT audit, GDPR, and CCPA.
* Identify relevant technology and industry developments, including ITIL 4, ServiceNow, and DevOps practices, and assess their value to Hertz.
* Communicate service performance, risks, priorities, and improvement plans clearly to executives, business partners, employees, and vendors.

**What We’re Looking For:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Computer Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
* ITIL 4 certification preferred;

Reporting to the CFO, the VP of Global Technology leads our Global Technology organization and sets JR286’s strategic direction for Enterprise Systems, Data, Platforms, Tools and AI. Karman Space & Defense is a leader in the rapid design, development, and production of critical, next-generation system solutions that align with the U.S. Department of War and its allies' core mission priorities, and meet the accelerating demand for access to space. Building on nearly 50 years of success, we deliver Payload & Protection Systems, Aero/Hydrodynamic Interstage Systems, and Propulsion & Launch Systems to more than 80 prime contractors supporting over 130 space and defense programs.

The Director of Production Planning leads the enterprise production planning and scheduling operating system across Karman's manufacturing operations. In this role, you will transform customer demand and Sales, Inventory and Operations Planning (SIOP) outputs into executable production plans, capacity strategies, and recovery actions that support on-time delivery and predictable execution while providing visibility into risks, constraints, and opportunities across the manufacturing network.

**Responsibilities**

* Leads production planning, master scheduling, and finite-capacity planning across Karman manufacturing sites and value streams.
* Translates customer demand, backlog, and Sales, Inventory and Operations Planning (SIOP) outputs into achievable production schedules with clear priorities, constraints, and recovery plans.
* Establishes planning standards and key performance indicators (KPIs) for schedule adherence, on-time delivery, past-due backlog, work-in-process (WIP) aging, capacity utilization, and plan attainment.
* Partners with Operations and Manufacturing Engineering to align labor, equipment, tooling, and process capacity with production requirements.
* Coordinates with Supply Chain to identify material shortages, supplier constraints, and outside-processing risks before they affect production performance.
* Leads schedule recovery and re-baselining efforts when demand, material availability, quality issues, or capacity changes create delivery risk.
* Ensures enterprise resource planning (ERP), material requirements planning (MRP), and planning data are accurate, timely, and aligned with approved operating plans.
* Develops planners and schedulers while building a high-accountability planning organization.
* Provides executive visibility into delivery risk, capacity gaps, staffing needs, and critical decisions required to protect customer commitments.
* Improves end-to-end SIOP, planning, scheduling, and production-control processes.

* Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Operations, Engineering, Business, or a related field.
* 10+ years of production planning, master scheduling, operations planning, or supply chain experience in a manufacturing environment.
* 5+ years of leadership experience managing planning, scheduling, or production-control teams.

**Description**

Leidos is hiring a Director of DevOps to lead the engineering organization's delivery platform: the pipeline that takes software from a developer's commit to a signed, approved release across commercial cloud and accredited government environments. The role is a people-leadership position that reports to the Senior Vice President, Engineering.

**What this role will deliver**
-------------------------------

The Director will deliver a single, trusted release pipeline that takes every engineering team's software, whether enterprise applications or hardware-bound and machine learning workloads, from commit to approved release, with full provenance (a verifiable record of how the software was built) and built-in security evidence, so that accreditation and security reviews draw on data the pipeline already produced. Commercial cloud and accredited government environments will be consistent and reproducible, so a build that passes in one behaves the same in the other.

Production services will run to published reliability targets, with working observability and a well-run on-call practice, and every significant incident will end in a blameless review with tracked fixes. Engineering teams will see shorter lead times through standard, self-service tooling, and leadership will get release-readiness data early enough to inform go or no-go decisions.

The Director will also build and retain a high-performing team of DevOps, site reliability and release engineers, manage vendor and partner relationships, and keep cloud and compute spend within budget.

**Location:** The ideal candidate will be based in Northern Virginia or near another Leidos facility, such as Huntsville, AL, or San Diego, CA. Onsite work at a Leidos facility is required as business needs dictate.

**Required qualifications**
---------------------------

* Active Top Secret clearance, with the ability to obtain Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) access
* Experience leading DevOps, site reliability engineering or platform teams, with the ability to hire, develop and lead engineers, manage a budget, work with vendors and partners, and influence senior executives
* Proven record of designing and running continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines at scale, backed by measurable gains in lead time, deployment frequency, change failure rate and recovery time
* Hands-on experience in software supply chain security, including software bills of materials, artifact signing, provenance and vulnerability management in a regulated environment
* Deep technical experience with commercial cloud platforms and infrastructure as code, containers and Kubernetes, and Linux systems administration
* Working knowledge of federal security and accreditation frameworks such as the Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP), National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Special Publication 800-53 and Department of Defense (DoD) cloud impact levels

Are you into solving tough problems and building cool tech? Do you thrive in a team where your ideas are heard and your creativity is encouraged? If you're nodding along, Mile 2 might be the place for you.

We're all about creating advanced solutions that really make a difference for our government partners. Our team uses the latest technologies to make a tangible impact, creating seamless integrations between human expertise and machine capabilities to tackle complex challenges.

Our core values guide everything we do: Supported Autonomy: We trust you to take initiative and make decisions, but we've always got your back. Humble Expertise: We respect everyone's knowledge and skills, creating an environment where we can all learn and get better together. Success is a Team Effort: We believe that we can only achieve great things when we work as a team. When you join us, you'll work on meaningful projects that challenge you and help you grow. We offer a supportive and inclusive environment, competitive benefits, and plenty of opportunities to advance your career. The ideal candidate is a technically credible, strategically minded professional who thrives at the intersection of mission requirements, emerging technologies, and business development. This individual translates complex customer challenges into innovative, executable solutions, leads technical and capture activities across the business development lifecycle, and develops compelling written proposals that communicate Mile 2's value and competitive differentiation.

This is a hands-on leadership position that requires both strategic thinking and direct execution. The Director is expected to personally develop technical solutions, author substantive proposal content, manage assigned capture activities, and produce the deliverables necessary to advance opportunities. Success requires the ability to move seamlessly between developing strategy, coordinating contributors, and executing the work. As a senior member of the Growth organization, the Director works closely with Growth leadership, the Chief Technology Officer, engineering teams, program leadership, and external partners to develop competitive solutions and advance strategic pursuits.

Nashville Predators Job Description
  
  
**Job Title:** Director, Hockey Systems
  
**Department:** Hockey Operations
  
**Job Reports To:** Assistant to the General Manager
  
**Status:** Exempt
  
  
About the Role
  
The Nashville Predators are seeking a Director of Hockey Systems to lead the data platform and applications supporting our coaching, scouting, and player evaluation staff.
  
  
This position will own the systems that carry hockey data from collection to decision: the pipelines, the data warehouse, and the internal web application staff use every day. This position will also build and lead a team of engineers, set the department's technical standards, and work alongside the Directors of Hockey Analytics and Hockey Research & Development.
  
  
Responsibilities
  

* Own the department's data platform, including ingestion, storage, orchestration, and monitoring.
* Build and maintain pipelines for event, tracking, and league data across the NHL and AHL, along with Junior, College, and European leagues.
* Manage the technical relationship with data vendors, including new feeds and changes to existing ones.
* Lead the design and development of the internal web application that coaches, scouts, and Hockey Operations staff use for player and team information.
* Take models from Research and Development into production.
* Set standards for code quality, testing, documentation, and data quality across the department.
* Own access control and data security for Hockey Operations systems.
* Lead Hockey Operations' use of AI tools in software and application development.
* Hire, lead, and develop the department's engineers, including code review and project assignment.
* Advise Hockey Operations leadership on technology decisions.
* Work with Analytics and Research and Development to set priorities and turn staff requests into a delivery plan.

Minimum Requirements
  

* Minimum of 3-7 years in software or data engineering, including experience leading projects or people.
* Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
* Advanced SQL and data modeling, including schema design for analytical databases and warehouses.
* Experience building and maintaining ETL/ELT pipelines in Python, including orchestration, monitoring, and data-quality checks.
* Experience with at least one cloud platform (AWS, Azure, or GCP).
* Experience with CI/CD, version control, code review, and automated testing.
* Experience building and shipping a web application that people use daily.
* Written and verbal communication skills suited to non-technical audiences and senior decision-makers.
* As a condition of employment, qualified applicant will be subject to a background check, including a criminal history check, driver history and character references.
* Possess a valid driver’s license, possess a suitable driving history and be insurable by the Organization’s insurance carrier.

Summary
  
  
The National Cancer Institute (NCI) is seeking an innovative leader to serve as the Director, Center for Biomedical Informatics and Information Technology (CBIIT), located in the Office of the Director (OD), National Cancer Institute (NCI), National Institutes of Health (NIH). The Director, CBIIT is classified under the Title 42 hiring mechanism and is equivalent to an extramural Program Division Director position. The position reports to the NCI Deputy Director for Data Science and Strategy. The Director, CBIIT leads the federal government components in the cancer research IT and informatics enterprise. In this capacity, the CBIIT Director delivers executive and managerial leadership and oversight for NCI-wide cybersecurity, use of IT, alignment with federal IT policies and requirements. The position also provides data science and informatics vision to NCI data science, informatics, and computational investments, including advancing the use of artificial intelligence across the research and operational spectrum. The Director, CBIIT oversees the implementation of the NCI cancer data ecosystem, the function of the NCI CIO, and coordinates data science and research data access for NCI at a national level.
  
Duties
  
  
The Director, CBIIT, is responsible for oversight of critical NCI information systems including systems that support clinical trials data, cancer data standards, multimodal cancer research data, and NCI grants information and other key business systems. The position manages a budget of approximately $240 million dollars, overseeing a federal workforce of approximately 90 people and more than 600 contractors engaged in providing IT, biomedical research informatics and software infrastructure and services to NCI. The CBIIT Director also participates in the scientific leadership of NCI and in NCI research initiatives and represents NCI with relevant national and international research communities. The CBIIT Director will also build strong working relationships that foster a strong, vibrant cohesive team across NCI.
  
  
For more information on CBIIT, visit https://www.cancer.gov/about-nci/organization/cbiit
  
  
NCI is based in Montgomery County, MD however location can be negotiable .

The National Institutes of Health (NIH), Office of the Director (OD), is seeking an exceptional scientific leader for the position of Deputy Director in the Office of Research Infrastructure Programs (ORIP) in the Division of Program Coordination, Planning, and Strategic Initiatives (DPCPSI), Office of the Director, NIH. (6) support training and career development for research veterinarians and other specialized professionals essential to comparative medicine and biomedical research; (7) support the acquisition of state-of-the-art scientific instrumentation and integrated instrument systems that expand access to advanced technologies and strengthen research capacity; **About the Department**

The Clinical, Medical and Regulatory (CMR) department at Novo Nordisk is one of the most diverse and collaborative groups within the organization. From healthcare provider interactions and developing and implementing regulatory strategies with the FDA to providing medical education and collecting data to support efficacy and new product development, CMR is involved. The one thing that keeps us all marching to the same beat is our patient centered focus. At Novo Nordisk, you will help patients around the world. As their needs evolve, so does our challenge to find better and more innovative ways to improve their quality of life. We’re changing lives for a living. Are you ready to make a difference?

  

**The Position**

As a senior member of the Biostatistics, Clinical Analytics & Modelling (BCAM) team, the Associate Data Science Director conceptualizes, defines, and delivers advanced data & analytics as well as AI/LLM solutions within the scope of the Clinical Data Science and Evidence (CDSE) group.

The role interfaces with various stakeholders across Health Economics and Outcomes Research (HEOR), Real-World Evidence (RWE), Medical Affairs, Clinical Trials Operations, Market Access, and other teams to deliver on analytics undertakings that may range from: (i) fast-turnaround, hands-on execution of insights on healthcare data; (ii) independently lead the execution of observational research studies through the hands-on analysis of real world data sources and application of appropriate data science and statistical techniques; (iii) build AI/LLM capabilities aimed at improving the team’s technology stack; (iv) serves as a subject matter expert in biostatistics on the design of HEOR studies, post-hoc analysis of clinical trial data, and analytical insights.

Within that spectrum, the role handles RWD from various sources including open and closed Medical Claims, EHR/EMR, Lab Results, Census, CDC Survey data (e.g., NHANES) as well as internal systems of record, translating findings into clear, compelling data stories.

The toolkit spans the programming languages SQL (Snowflake, Databricks), R, Python, Tableau as well as cutting-edge AI/LLM capabilities, including Anthropic's Claude Code ecosystem of marketplaces, plugins, Skills, (sub) agents, MCP servers, and hooks. A key mission of this role is to reimagine how healthcare Data Science and Real-World Evidence & Insights are programmatically generated by co-leading the continuous development and evolution of the AI workflow and technology stack that supports the BCAM team.

  

**Relationships**

Reports to the Sr. Director, Biostatistics, Clinical Analytics, & Modelling (BCAM), which is part of CDSE. This is a US affiliate role aligned with US business needs. **Company Overview**

Orbis is a technology company that delivers sovereign intelligence and decision capabilities to the United States Government and its allies. We convert complex information and operational systems into decisive outcomes, giving public institutions and critical enterprises the tools to move faster, see clearer, and act first in an increasingly contested world.

We are not a consulting firm and not a systems integrator. Every Orbis team is built around practitioners who have operated at the mission edge, and every engagement is judged on one thing: whether it produces working capability, not slide decks. Solutions forged from experience; that is how we build, and it is how we hire.

**Job Summary**

Orbis is looking for a **Technical Director** for **FMS and International Programs** to drive enablement for a program deploying Orbis Catalyst as a sovereign data fabric for an international government defense client. The program spans enterprise and tactical edge, integrates the client's full sensor and platform inventory across every warfighting domain, and runs under the client's sovereign authority. **Make a Difference in YOUR Career!**

Our vision is both simple and ambitious: to put our drinks on every table.

We are the leading global independent beverage solutions provider. We serve a broad range of national and international retailers as well as Global, National and Emerging (GNE) brands. Our products are distributed worldwide from our production sites in Europe, North America, and Australia. Although our own branding may not appear on the labels of the beverages we produce, there is a good chance you are reading this while sipping one of our drinks.

Our ambition is to continually improve and it’s what keeps us at the top of our game. We are solutions-based. We are innovative. We seek out new challenges and conquer them. This is our company ethos, but it’s our people’s too: Refresco is at the cutting edge of a fast-moving industry because we have passionate people pushing the boundaries of what’s best.

Stop and think: how would **YOU** put our drinks on every table?

**Summary Description:**

* Reporting to the Vice President of Engineering and Project Management, the Director of Engineering drives improvements within the operations maintenance organization across 5+ facilities in the assigned region of Refresco NA. This role is responsible for advancing production technologies by applying sound maintenance and reliability principles. This role also ensures the effective execution of capital projects, equipment reliability, and continuous improvement initiatives to drive operational excellence. The Director of Engineering directly manages a team of Project Engineering Managers, each responsible for overseeing engineering efforts across multiple facilities within their assigned regions.

**Essential Functions:**

* Develop a support organization capable of managing plant maintenance operations regionally in US and Canada.
* Deliver criteria to determine whether the Maintenance Organization is fulfilling the needs of each Plant.
* Develop and manage engineering and maintenance budgets across all locations, ensuring effective resource allocation for seasonal rebuilds, equipment needs, and capital projects. Monitor expenses to optimize costs and maintain alignment with company financial objectives.
* Oversee the planning, execution, and prioritization of plant-driven capital projects to ensure alignment with company standards, cost-effectiveness, and business needs.
* Collaborate with cross-functional teams to develop and implement new initiatives that enhance capacity, flexibility, cost efficiency, and quality across facilities.
* Provide strategic oversight on staffing, performance management, and workforce planning to meet business objectives.
* Lead the implementation of SAP Maintenance throughout the system.
* Other duties as assigned, including special projects that may require significant travel to manufacturing plant locations.
* Work as an integral member of the engineering, maintenance and Infrastructure design and installation

Hybrid

***Job Overview***

Rel aiR is the high-scale, secure, and defensible platform where legal data lives. It runs on infrastructure that has to be available, economical, and compliant in every region we serve. We hold more than 100 petabytes of customer data today, and we are building for hundreds of petabytes in the next three years, scaling potentially to an exabyte within five. This is sensitive data at scale, and managing it requires a global understanding of data management.
  
  
The load is rising from multiple directions at once. More legal work is being done with the help of AI-driven software. AI is supporting more use cases across Legal Data Intelligence. MCP (Model Context Protocol) and third-party builder programs are automating more workflows. And we are moving all new matters to Rel aiR. We are hiring a Vice President of Core Infrastructure to build the foundation for that growth and to join the leadership team of Engineering at Relativity. You will own SQL platform, compute (Kubernetes), reliability and operations, and incident and problem management, and build a new capacity-forecasting function.
  
  
Your strategy will span multiple data centers and multiple ways to store data. You will stay agile when cloud storage capacity is tight, adapt to data sovereignty and local requirements around the world, and work with Security to keep the fortress secure. You will work with engineering teams to raise utilization and route work to the resources available, and you will make sure we use services that meet our economic targets, and use them well.
