- Establish value-based prioritization criteria (financial impact, feasibility, risk, strategic fit, readiness) and lead governance forums that make clear investment decisions.
- Maintain an enterprise view of AI initiatives to reduce duplication, surface dependencies, and direct resources to the highest-value work.
Opportunity assessment and solutioning
- Lead structured assessment of process and project candidates, including current-state analysis, business case development, build/buy/partner evaluation, and solution feasibility.
- Shape solution architectures with technology, data, and vendor partners, balancing speed, cost, scalability, and control.
- Match each opportunity to the right AI approach (generative AL, machine learning, intelligent automation, or no AI at all), validating data readiness, technical feasibility, and guides solution from proof of concept to production ready design.
- Challenge and sharpen proposals: separate genuine transformation opportunities from automation for its own sake.
Transformation delivery
- Lead cross-functional programs from proof of concept to production, partnering with Technology, Data, Operations, Product, and business lines.
- Stand up and mature the program management infrastructure: stage gates, delivery standards, benefits tracking, and executive reporting.
- Drive operating model, process, and role redesign so that AI capabilities are embedded in how work actually gets done.
- Own change management, training, and adoption strategy, with accountability for realized benefits rather than deployments alone.
Governance, risk, and compliance
- Partner with Risk, Compliance, Legal, Information Security, and Model Risk Management to embed responsible AI practices, including data privacy

Position Overview:
The Director of Data & Analytics is ExploreK12's senior data leader, reporting to the VP of Engineering. The Director leads the team responsible for how company data is modeled, governed, and delivered across the enterprise, including data engineering, analytics, business intelligence, reporting, and Data & Analytics' contribution to adaptive-learning capabilities.

The Director leads a working Senior Manager responsible for adaptive logic and analysis, a PM / BA / Scrum Master, and data engineers supporting enterprise and product needs. The Director is accountable for the overall technical direction, architecture, delivery, and development of the Data & Analytics organization while remaining directly involved in the team's most important technical work.

This is a working Director role. The Director must be able to open any model in the repository, reason about its design and implementation without a translator, and contribute directly to complex or ambiguous technical work. A candidate who intends to step away from the code is not a fit for this role.

- Lead the Data & Analytics organization, including a Senior Manager, PM / BA / Scrum Master, and data engineers, with accountability for organizational performance, talent development, hiring, and developing engineers' technical and modeling judgment.
- Set the data roadmap with the VP of Engineering within the broader technology and data strategy, prioritizing initiatives based on business value, cost, risk, and capacity.
- Serve as a trusted data partner to business, product, and BU leaders, providing credible feasibility, cost, and trade-off assessments before work begins.
- Treat data as a product: understand the users and requirements for data assets and manage the warehouse, models, reporting, and dashboards with clear ownership, quality standards, and measures of success.
- Own data architecture and engineering standards, including warehouse design, modeling conventions, shared codebase standards, and use of curated data layers; use design and code reviews to ensure quality and develop team judgment.
- Build deep knowledge of source data across product lines and lead reconciliation of metrics and sources of truth across legacy systems.
- Ensure Data & Analytics' contribution to adaptive logic and analysis is well governed and coordinated with Product and other teams that share this work.
- Represent Data & Analytics on the Data Governance Committee and translate governance, privacy, and security requirements into platform controls and practices, including access controls, the data glossary and catalog, PII tagging, and lineage.

Product Design Director, Strategic Futures, Customer Experience Platforms (CXP)

R1004316
We’re seeking a talented Product Designer Individual Contributor (IC) at a Director level to lead for our Strategic Future team in Customer Experience Platforms (CXP) Design org, part of the Experience Design organization. The Strategic Future Tier of CXP sets the multi-year trajectory for Capital One’s digital products, defining the future of our 1st-party experiences and 3rd-party integrations while establishing high-level intent and capability requirements for the ecosystem.

The Experience Design team at Capital One is at the forefront of enriching our customers’ digital and physical experiences and we are passionate about creating memorable, meaningful product experiences that build the Capital One brand with humanity and drive business advantage and innovation. We champion a thriving environment of collaboration, authenticity and healthy critique, in which we honor diversity of thought, create a culture of belonging, and elevate one another. If you’re a creative innovator who embraces an environment where you can experiment, learn, and change banking for good, we’d love to hear from you.

Role Expectations
As an IC Director on the Strategic Future team, you’ll be part of a cross-disciplinary team of designers and collaborate deeply with our research teams, content design, and Product and Tech leadership. You’ll be responsible for leading high-impact, highly complex projects and designing and building rich interactive prototypes of innovative future customer experiences.

Here are some of the expected competencies for this role:

Product Design Expertise: Apply your established design and leadership skills to elevate the quality and maturity of the Capital One experience. Leveraging a variety of hard skills across interaction, visual and service design, you'll apply and optimize the use of appropriate tools, platforms, frameworks and design systems that enables your team to solve complex problems and explain their solutions using a variety of design artifacts that may include vision stories, journey maps, blueprints, high-fidelity designs and prototypes

AI Experience: Leverage AI technologies from process through output to positively shift your team’s velocity and outcomes. Deliver AI that transforms a human experience for good, packaged in compelling storytelling

Leadership: Create conditions for a positive and inclusive team environment and set a vision for an inclusive, collaborative culture that makes your team feel valued and heard

Human-Centered: Champion voices of both customers and partners, modeling the mindset that business and customer outcomes are not distinct but complementary, ultimately resulting in experiences that exceed baseline customer needs and expectations

workday:capital one:R1005777.description:
Senior Director, Data Engineer

As a Senior Director, Data Engineer at Capital One, you will lead high-performing engineering teams working to define the future of data platforms and banking in the cloud. You will partner closely with product managers, data scientists, architects and executive leaders to deliver scalable, data-driven solutions. Our Senior Directors are technical people leaders who drive data engineering strategy, guide complex architectural decisions and translate business goals into impactful data platforms.

At Capital One, we believe diversity of thought strengthens our ability to influence, collaborate and provide the most innovative solutions across organizational boundaries. You will foster a culture of engineering excellence and inclusivity, balancing technical depth with empowered team leadership. You will lead the way in building next-generation talent for Capital One Tech—mentoring managers and engineers, driving workforce strategy and actively recruiting top-tier talent.

Senior Directors are expected to lead through technical vision, operational rigor and strategic alignment. You will serve as a key owner for your domain's technical health, delivery velocity and system resilience. While shaping long-term data strategy and platform roadmaps, you will inspire a culture of continuous learning, innovation and high-impact delivery across your organization.

What You’ll Do:
- Lead, manage, and grow multiple teams of product-focused software and data engineers
- Embrace and incubate emerging technology and open-source products across all platforms
- Work to modernize our existing tech stacks and data platforms
- Collaborate with internal teams to find areas of opportunities for automation and machine learning
- Partner with architects, product owners, data professionals, and software and data engineers to drive the implementation of new applications
- Work within and across Agile teams to design, develop, test, implement and support technical solutions across full-stack development tools and technologies
- Lead efforts to deploy new and existing applications into AWS environments and provide operational support for the applications
- Conduct design and code reviews to ensure compliance with standards
- Serve as an ambassador for the data engineering team, communicating technical concepts and data outcomes clearly to both internal and external stakeholders to drive alignment and shared understanding
- Oversee the design and health of data platforms and pipelines, establishing standards for scalability, resilience, and operational efficiency, ensuring robust performance under increasing data volume and business demands
- Serve as a force-multiplier for the team, balancing deep, hands-on technical contribution and innovation with mentoring and elevating the skills of peers and junior engineers
- Lead and execute large-scale, transformative data initiatives from end to end, independently driving critical architectural decisions

workday:capital one:R1005783.description:
Staff Full Stack Engineer (Director Level)

As a Staff Engineer at Capital One, you will be part of a community of technical experts working to define the future of banking in the cloud. You will work alongside our talented team of developers, machine learning experts, product managers and people leaders. Our Staff Engineers are leading experts in their domains, helping devise practical and reusable solutions to complex problems. You will drive innovation at multiple levels, helping optimize business outcomes while delivering strong technology solutions.

At Capital One, we believe diversity of thought strengthens our ability to influence, collaborate and provide the most innovative solutions across organizational boundaries. You will promote a culture of engineering excellence and strike the right balance between lending expertise and providing an inclusive environment where the ideas of others can be heard and championed. You will lead the way in creating next-generation talent for Capital One Tech, mentoring engineers and actively recruiting to keep building our community.

Staff Engineers are expected to lead through technical contribution. You will operate as a trusted advisor for our key technologies, platforms and capability domains, creating clear and concise communications, code samples, blog posts and other materials to share knowledge both inside and outside the organization. You will specialize in a particular subject area, but your input and impact will be sought and expected throughout the organization.

What You’ll Do:
- Articulate and evangelize a bold technical vision for your domain
- Decompose complex problems into practical and operational solutions
- Ensure the quality of technical design and implementation
- Serve as an authoritative expert on non-functional system characteristics, such as performance, scalability and operability
- Continue learning and injecting advanced technical knowledge into our community

About the Role
The Director, Product Engineering will lead the team responsible for our care management applications and the vendor integrations that connect them to the rest of the care ecosystem, including EHRs, scheduling systems, and other external health systems. The Director will manage a team of engineering managers and senior engineers, while serving as a hands-on technical leader who sets the standard through their own contributions to the code.

We’ve embraced AI to empower our engineers, using Cursor and agentic tooling for triage, automated updates, and faster feature delivery. The Director will partner closely with product, design, clinical operations, data science, and data platform teams to deliver technology that drives tech-enabled care for underserved populations. We’re looking for a leader who is equally comfortable growing people and writing code, and who is deeply curious about, and energized by, what AI-first engineering makes possible.

- Design and maintain the guardrails, validation processes, and review personas that allow agents to safely run the full development lifecycle
- Shift the team’s focus from hand-building features to designing, evaluating, and improving the agentic systems that build them

At The Coca‑Cola Company, sustainability is core to how we refresh the world and make a difference. As we advance our transformation into a consumer‑centric total beverage company, we’re committed to creating shared value across customers, consumers, and communities.

This leader shapes the roadmap for customer and consumer sustainability initiatives—advancing packaging, water, and climate goals while enabling growth across brands and retail channels. The ideal candidate blends sustainability fluency with commercial acumen, cross‑functional collaboration, and strategic storytelling to translate sustainability into tangible business and brand value.

- Build sustainability capability across customer teams by equipping them with frameworks, tools, and best practices for sustainability planning and engagement.
- Co‑lead programs integrating sustainability performance into customer scorecards and planning cycles.

- Collaborate with Consumer Value Creation, Brand, and Marketing teams to bring sustainability into consumer programs and campaigns that strengthen brand perception and purchase intent.
- Partner with Strategic Property and Asset teams to embed sustainability storytelling into high‑impact consumer experiences and brand touchpoints.
- Use consumer insights to develop communication strategies that connect sustainability actions with brand relevance and loyalty.
- Measurement, Capability, and Scaling:
- Establish shared measurement systems demonstrating customer and consumer sustainability outcomes and commercial impact.

- Share learnings and build organizational capability through workshops, engagement sessions, and cross‑system collaboration.

At Columbia, we're as passionate about the outdoors as you are. And while our gear is available worldwide, we're proud to be based in the Pacific Northwest, where natural wonders are our playground.

Every product we make and every task we undertake is inspired by the famous words of our founder, Gert Boyle: "It's perfect. Now make it better." As pioneers of relentless improvement, we are constantly evolving.

We believe the outdoors is ours to protect and strive to keep our planet healthy. We believe in empowering people to experience the outdoors to the fullest.

And we believe in you.

Working in a highly collaborative model with the Head of Operational Development Excellence & Engineering, the role translates business requirements into technology solutions while maintaining clear accountability for technology architecture, application delivery, systems integration, platform operations, cybersecurity, and technical support.

The Senior Director owns the technology strategy and roadmap for logistics platforms including warehouse management, warehouse execution, warehouse control, transportation management, labor management, automation integration, visibility, and supporting supply chain technologies. The role is accountable for the successful design, implementation, operation, and continuous improvement of these platforms across company-managed and partner-managed distribution environments.

We're committed to bringing passion and customer focus to the business.

The Director of Program Management leads the site's program management team, balancing customer, and organizational needs by translating them into actionable strategies. Acting as the voice of the customer internally and the business externally, the Director drives account strategies to achieve revenue and profitability goals.

This role develops customer strategies, aligns with functional teams, and standardizes processes. Collaborating with Business Development, the Director oversees proposal preparation, monitors project plans for new and existing customers, and reviews Customer Focused Team (CFT) metrics to improve customer service, financial performance, cost, quality, delivery, and value-added opportunities.

As a key leadership team member, the Director manages a diverse portfolio of customer accounts, sets professional standards for the Program Management function, and drives strategic initiatives with a long-term impact on business performance.
DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES include, but not limited to:

• Lead the program management team by setting clear goals, holding team members accountable, and providing direction.

• Manage account program operations within a CFT matrix, collaborating across production, planning, materials, quality, engineering, and business development functions.

• Equip Program Managers with tools and training to deliver on time and within budget, while supporting pricing strategies for new business opportunities.

• Ensure effective management of operational metrics such as on-time delivery, quality, responsiveness, cost, and technology usage, addressing deviations with corrective actions.

• Build and foster a high-performing team that drives revenue growth, meets financial targets, and cultivates a culture of excellence and innovation.

• Mentor Program Managers in stakeholder alignment, communication, meeting leadership, and customer updates.

• Oversee program expenditures, budget planning, revenue and material forecasting, and Profit & Loss (P&L) variance resolution, ensuring Return on Investment (ROI) and financial performance.

• Lead program quoting and requoting activities, conduct financial and operational reviews, and present during Customer Strategic Business Reviews.

• Support the execution of new programs to meet budget, schedule, and technical goals while identifying new business opportunities within existing accounts.

• Travel as required (up to 10%).

• Other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS:
Education and Required Experience

• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and experience. Masters (Communications, Business or Finance) desired.

• 10+ Years of progressive EMS experience, with a proven track record of success in leading complex projects.

Crescent is a differentiated U.S. energy company committed to delivering value through a disciplined, returns-driven growth through acquisition strategy and consistent return of capital. Our long-life, balanced portfolio combines significant cash flow from stable production with a deep, high-quality development inventory. Crescent is a top three producer in the Eagle Ford basin and a scaled operator in each of the Permian and Uinta basins. Crescent’s leadership is an experienced team of investment, financial and industry professionals that combines proven investment and operating expertise. For more than a decade, Crescent and our predecessors have executed on a consistent strategy focused on cash flow, risk management and returns. Through disciplined and accretive investments, we have successfully tripled the size of our company since going public in December 2021 while maintaining a strong balance sheet.

The Director of Enterprise Services is a technology leader responsible for building, leading, and continuously improving the foundational IT services that enable Crescent Energy’s business operations and future growth. This role oversees enterprise infrastructure and cloud operations, networking, service desk, and digital end-user experience, ensuring reliable, secure, scalable, and cost-effective technology services across the organization.

As a key member of the IT leadership team, this individual will develop a high-performing team, establish operational excellence, and build strong partnerships with business stakeholders, technology peers, and strategic vendors. The Director will strengthen Crescent’s technology foundation through standardized processes, clear accountability, service-oriented delivery, and continuous improvement. Significant upstream exploration and production (E&P) experience is essential. The ideal candidate combines strong technical understanding with exceptional people leadership, operational discipline, and a pragmatic approach to modernization, while understanding the distributed operations, acquisition activity, and business requirements of an independent upstream company.

- Build, lead, recruit, mentor, and develop a high-performing team spanning infrastructure and cloud operations, networking, service desk, and end-user services.

- Develop technical talent and emerging leaders, strengthening succession planning and the team’s ability to scale with Crescent.
- Foster a culture of customer service, operational excellence, stewardship, integrity, teamwork, and continuous improvement.
- Collaborate closely with IT peers and business leaders to ensure integrated, business-aligned technology services.

- Creating competitive, actuarially sound pricing solutions that support sustainable growth and strengthen market positioning.

Members should not have to call us to understand their claims, benefits, or what they owe. - Define a clear product vision for health finances self-service across Commercial, Medicare, and Medicaid members.

- Monitor market trends, regulatory changes, and emerging technologies, incorporating innovations that enhance the member experience.

- Lead PI Planning and agile ceremonies to ensure alignment, transparency, and effective execution across teams.
- Oversee product launches and ensure adoption plans, measurement strategies, and feedback loops are established from day one.

GENERAL PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The Senior Director, Technical Delivery – Integrated Kidney Care (IKC) is accountable for the overarching technology delivery strategy, execution, and operational governance across DaVita’s Value-Based Care (VBC) ecosystem. This role spearheads the end-to-end engineering, integration, and operational reliability of digital platforms supporting comprehensive care for Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) and End-Stage Kidney Disease (ESKD) populations.

Leading through a layer of senior managers and managers, this executive oversees cross-functional delivery organizations spanning:
- Epic EHR Ecosystem: Foundational aspects of Epic’s platform offerings, along with Epic Care Everywhere, interoperability protocols (HL7, FHIR, XDR), and provider engagement tools.
- Custom Engineering Applications: Cloud-native care management platforms, clinical data pipelines, digital tools for multidisciplinary care teams (including clinician/care coordinator applications, provider and patient portals), and bespoke service architectures.
- Artificial Intelligence & Advanced Analytics: Production AI/ML integration, including predictive risk scoring, clinical decision support, conversational AI assistants, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) knowledge systems for clinical guidelines, and automated clinical documentation/workflow intelligence.

The Company
Dexcom Corporation (NASDAQ DXCM) is a pioneer and global leader in continuous glucose monitoring (CGM). Dexcom began as a small company with a big dream: To forever change how diabetes is managed. To unlock information and insights that drive better health outcomes. Here we are 25 years later, having pioneered an industry. And we're just getting started. We are broadening our vision beyond diabetes to empower people to take control of health. That means personalized, actionable insights aimed at solving important health challenges. To continue what we've started: Improving human health.

We are driven by thousands of ambitious, passionate people worldwide who are willing to fight like warriors to earn the trust of our customers by listening, serving with integrity, thinking big, and being dependable. We've already changed millions of lives and we're ready to change millions more. Our future ambition is to become a leading consumer health technology company while continuing to develop solutions for serious health conditions. We'll get there by constantly reinventing unique biosensing-technology experiences. Though we've come a long way from our small company days, our dreams are bigger than ever. The opportunity to improve health on a global scale stands before us.

The Senior Director, Software & Services Strategy will report directly to the VP, Strategy, Power and serve as the enterprise strategist and business architect for the convergence of software, controls, industrial data, artificial intelligence, and lifecycle services across the Power Segment.

·  The most important future customer outcomes span organizational boundaries and cannot be captured by Services, Software & Controls Solutions, Engineering, or Digital Technology acting independently.
·  Industrial software firms, systems integrators, hyperscalers, OEMs, and AI-native entrants are increasingly competing to own the customer’s data context, workflow layer, decision interface, and transformation agenda.
·  GE Vernova’s differentiated starting point is its installed base, controls authority, equipment and fleet knowledge, service history, customer relationships, and ability to translate insight into safe, validated action.
·  Without coordinated leadership, fragmented investment, unclear commercial credit, competing roadmaps, and slow cross-business decisions could prevent Power from converting those assets into durable growth.
·  The role creates a single point of accountability for translating the strategy into a portfolio of customer-backed ventures and scalable operating-model choices.

Mission
Build the strategy, operating model, partnerships, commercial architecture, and transformation portfolio required for Software, Controls, AI, Industrial Data, and Services to operate as one integrated growth system.

Job Description
Ready to take your career global?

Make your mark at one of the biggest names in payments. We’re looking for a Director, Transformation & Corporate Strategy to join our ever evolving team and help shape the future of global commerce.

Global Payments' Transformation Office is a central, enterprise-wide function based in the company's Atlanta headquarters that partners closely with executive leadership to drive integration, growth, operating model, and cost transformation across the firm. The Transformation Office works across business units and functions to translate strategic priorities into executable transformation programs, establish enterprise transformation frameworks and operating cadence, and ensure disciplined value realization. The team partners with business unit, regional, and functional leadership to design scalable operating models, enable successful integration and separation, and drive sustainable growth and cost efficiency.

This role will be located at our Buckhead location in Atlanta, GA

What You Will Own
The Director, Transformation and Corporate Strategy is a leader within the Transformation Office, supporting the leader heading Corporate Strategy in Transformation Office and other senior transformation leaders on enterprise strategy, operating model, and transformation initiatives. Transformation Office is responsible for framing and solving the enterprise's hardest structural questions: where the operating model should change, how the organization should be designed to deliver it, and what it takes to make the change stick. The role suits an engagement manager from a top-tier consulting firm who wants to lead projects end to end, from problem definition and hypothesis development through analysis, recommendation, executive alignment, and implementation.

Problem structuring and engagement leadership:
- Translate ambiguous executive questions into defined workstreams with hypotheses, work plans, analytical approaches, and milestones.
- Target operating model design: lead operating model work across organization structure, governance, decision rights, capabilities, processes, service delivery, technology enablement, and performance management.
- Strategy development: evaluate growth, portfolio, product, market, and business model choices, and develop the fact base and reasoning that support a clear strategic direction.
- Structural alternatives: assess centralization, decentralization, shared services, centers of excellence, outsourcing, insourcing, and consolidation options, weighing cost, capability, risk, and speed rather than cost alone.
- Executive advisory and storylining: partner with senior executives to frame tradeoffs, challenge assumptions, and build synthesized recommendations for leadership forums.

Implementation and change:
- Translate recommendations into roadmaps, workstream charters, and adoption plans, and work with business leaders through the stakeholder, capability, and change management

Description -
Role Overview
It is an exciting time to join the Strategy and Planning team within HP’s Personal Systems group, a $37B business within an innovative Fortune 100 company. About Us:

insightsoftware is a global provider of reporting, analytics, and performance management solutions that unlock the potential of business data and transform the way finance and data teams operate. We empower leaders from over 32,000 organizations to make timely and intelligent decisions. Our comprehensive solutions span Financial Planning and Analysis (FP&A), Controllership, and Data and Analytics. We deliver finance teams the insights required to navigate any economic climate and drive greater financial intelligence, while increasing productivity, visibility, accuracy, and compliance. Learn more at insightsoftware.com.

Job Description:
As Vice President of Software Engineering for our Enterprise Performance Management (EPM) portfolio, you will lead a global organization of engineers across multiple product lines that finance teams rely on to plan, close, consolidate and report. You will own how that portfolio is built, shipped and run.

2027 is a transformation year. We are modernizing established applications, building new SaaS and multi-tenant capabilities, moving to an agentic software development lifecycle, and putting AI directly into the hands of our customers. We need a leader who can deliver all four at once without compromising the quality and reliability our customers depend on for their most critical financial processes, and who measures success with the same discipline our customers apply to their numbers.

We enjoy our work as much as we enjoy working together, and we want leaders who get things done while having a positive influence on our workplace environment.

What you will deliver in 2027

1. Modernize legacy applications
- Define and execute a modernization strategy for the EPM portfolio, choosing deliberately between re-platform, re-architect, strangler-pattern migration, and retirement for each product and component
- Sequence modernization to deliver customer value incrementally, avoiding big-bang rewrites and protecting customers already in production
- Reduce technical debt measurably, with a visible debt register, investment targets and progress reported to executive leadership
- Plan and execute customer migrations from on-premise and single-tenant deployments with clear data-integrity, cutover and rollback plans

2. Build SaaS and multi-tenant capabilities
- Lead the design and delivery of cloud-native, multi-tenant services, including tenant isolation, data partitioning, configuration and extensibility models
- Build the shared platform capabilities that product teams rely on: identity, observability, metering, tenant provisioning, and self-service environments
- Own SaaS operational excellence: SLOs and error budgets, on-call and incident management, capacity planning, cost efficiency, and disaster recovery
- Embed security, privacy and compliance (for example SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR) into architecture and delivery pipelines rather than treating them as downstream gates

Job Title: Sr. Director, Site Reliability Engineering

Manager/Supervisor: VP, Global Tech Ops/CISO

FLSA Status: Exempt

Position overview:
Insulet started in 2000 with an idea and a mission to enable our customers to enjoy simplicity, freedom, and healthier lives using our Omnipod® product platform. In the last two decades we have improved the lives of hundreds of thousands of patients by using innovative technology that is wearable, waterproof, and lifestyle accommodating.

This position requires a mix of strategic engineering and design along with hands-on, technical work. Your team will configure, tune, and tackle multi-tiered systems to achieve optimal application performance, stability, and availability. You will work closely with systems engineers, development and operations teams, and information security teams. Our Cloud systems enhance our ability to provide advanced solutions for people living with Diabetes. If you like a fast-paced environment and want your work to make a difference, Insulet is the place to be.

- Develop and maintain an effective working relationship with various levels of the organization, including business partners, management, and associates.
- Work closely with engineering managers, technical leads, architects, and development teams to ensure that platforms are designed with scale and operability in mind
- Develop a high performing team, recruiting as required, and guiding team members through performance management and personal career development.

Be a part of our mission! As a world leader in creating comfortable, sustainable, and efficient climate solutions for buildings, homes and transportation, it's our responsibility to put the planet first. For us at Trane Technologies , and through our businesses including Trane®  and  Thermo King ,  sustainability is not just how we do business—it is our business.  Do you dare to look at the world's challenges and see impactful possibilities?  Do you want to contribute to making a better future?  If the answer is yes, we invite you to consider joining us in boldly challenging what's possible for a sustainable world.

Learn about our benefits designed for you to thrive at work and at home.

We boldly go.

Where is the work:
Monday to Thursday, work onsite with your colleagues. Fridays, choose your work location, balancing what your work requires.

Join us as VP, Engineering and Technology , where you will provide thought leadership, influence and hands-on engagement in order to develop, direct, and implement the technology innovation agenda for Thermo King Americas business unit (BU) at Trane Technologies.  This role will report to the BU President for Thermo King Americas and work very closely with the SVP, Chief Technology and Sustainability Officer for Enterprise. This role will be on both the Thermo King Americas and Enterprise Engineering & Technology Leadership Teams.

This role will oversee the full spectrum of the technology and engineering continuum within Thermo King Americas, from advanced technology development to product, system and solution design and development, electrification, value engineering, product quality and reliability, and product/service commercialization in the areas of refrigerated transport and cold storage.  Working with Enterprise organizations, the VP, Engineering and Technology will be the driving force for engineering excellence to achieve the long-term business objectives and business growth aspirations globally.  The VP will be expected to elevate the innovation and project execution capabilities internally to the BU and Trane Technologies and through collaboration across the enterprise, alliances, partnerships and with other external constituents.

Who We Are
Johnson Controls is the global leader for smart, healthy and sustainable buildings. At Johnson Controls, we’ve been making buildings smarter since 1885, and our capabilities, depth of innovation experience, and global reach have been growing ever since. Today, we offer the world’s largest portfolio of building products, technologies, software, and services; we put that portfolio to work to transform the environments where people live, work, learn and play.

This is where Johnson Controls comes in, helping drive the outcomes that matter most. Through a full range of systems and digital solutions, we make your buildings smarter. A smarter building is safer, more comfortable, more efficient, and, ultimately, more sustainable. Most important, smarter buildings let you focus more intensely on your unique mission. Better for your people. Better for your bottom line. Better for the planet.

We’re helping to create a healthy planet with solutions that decrease energy use, reduce waste and make carbon neutrality a reality. Sustainability is a top priority for our company. We committed to invest 75 percent of new product development R&D in climate-related innovation to develop sustainable products and services. We take sustainability seriously.

Achieving net zero carbon emissions before 2040 is just one of our commitments to making the world a better place. Please visit and follow Johnson Controls for recent exciting activities.

Location: Flexible U.S.-based location near a Johnson Controls data center hub. Travel up to 50%.

AI is turning data centers into the most demanding buildings we have ever automated. Racks that drew 10 kilowatts a few years ago now draw more than 100, heat leaves the chip through water rather than air, and the control problem has moved from minutes to seconds. The people who build and run these sites want cooling that keeps every rack in its temperature band through load swings and failures, that lands on their own platforms and standards without rework, and that is proven in their own terms. Few vendors can do that across the whole thermal chain, from the cold plate to the chiller. Johnson Controls can, and this role leads it.

Moog’s Corporate IT’s Service Delivery Team is looking for a Director of Global Digital Workplace and End-User Services!

As a leader in these areas, you will have the authority to establish enterprise service standards, technology roadmaps, performance measures, escalation protocols, and supplier requirements for digital workplace and end-user services. The Corporate service teams own enterprise strategy, common platforms, governance, and service performance; local IT teams own on-site delivery, hands-on support, local relationships, and site-specific execution within those standards. You will align both groups to shift support from reactive issue resolution toward proactive reliability, automation, self-service, adoption, and measurable improvements in productivity and employee experience.

This role requires an onsite work schedule (five days in-office each week), at our Corporate Headquarters in East Aurora, NY.

- Bachelor’s degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Engineering, Business, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.

- Evidence of materially improving service reliability, restoration performance, employee satisfaction, technology adoption, or productivity while reducing repeat incidents and support friction.

- Ambiguity and decision enablement: Resolve ambiguity through structured problem solving; frame complex challenges, propose solutions, and guide sponsors and stakeholders to decisions and consensus
- Cross-functional influence: Lead and influence teams without direct reporting lines; partner with all functions affected by program deliverables, manage dependencies with legal, risk, and compliance, resolve conflicts, and secure accountability and commitment

Position Summary
The National Basketball Association (NBA) is seeking a strategic, highly collaborative, and technically credible Vice President, Cybersecurity Operations & Architecture to lead the design, operation, and continuous improvement of cybersecurity capabilities across the organization’s global technology ecosystem. Reporting directly to the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), this role serves as the senior leader accountable for integrating enterprise security architecture with day-to-day cyber defense, incident response, threat detection, and infrastructure protection.

The Vice President will establish security architecture strategy, standards, roadmaps, and reference architectures while ensuring those designs translate into sustainable operational controls, measurable detection coverage, effective response capabilities, and resilient technology services. The role will partner extensively with Cybersecurity, Enterprise Technology, Infrastructure, Engineering, Digital Products, Data & Analytics, Media Operations, Basketball Operations, Legal, Privacy, Compliance, NBA teams, arena operators, and external technology partners.

A core responsibility is setting NBA arena cybersecurity standards and making certain they are adhered to. We’re looking for a Senior Director of Product Management to own AI platform strategy at Nordstrom.

Internally, we are changing how thousands of Nordstrom employees do their jobs, from how engineers and product managers build software to how merchants, marketers and store teams operate. Externally, we are building the AI our customers experience directly across discovery, shopping and service. Both run on a shared foundation of platforms, tools and standards that have to be safe, usable and adopted at scale.

This leader owns that foundation: the shared AI platform capabilities the rest of the company builds on, so teams are not each solving the same problems from scratch. The scale of AI means some domain-level efforts will always be driven outside this leader’s direct scope, closest to the teams who need it. This role exists to make sure as much of that work as possible runs on common ground, and that the capabilities worth building once get built once and get used everywhere.

In this role, you will also oversee the data analysis and governance of the business, which directly enables the capabilities of the AI we will deploy internally. This leader will guide a team of data analysts and product managers who ensure the right data is available to users at the right time and from the right single sources of truth.

Strategy - Nordstrom’s AI platform strategy. Define the multi-year vision for our AI capabilities, platforms and tooling, and turn it into a sequenced, outcome-driven roadmap that senior leadership can fund and hold you to. Make the hard calls about what we build, what we buy and what we deliberately do not do.

Build AI That Could Help Transform the Future of Medicine

Frontier AI is changing what’s possible in science, and few places let you apply it to a problem as consequential as human health. Pfizer is one of them. We have decades of world-class biology and chemistry, rich biomedical data and the global reach to get medicines to patients. We are pairing them with the newest advances in AI and we are doing it along with the world’s leaders in building medicine.

At Pfizer, we believe the next generation of scientific breakthroughs will be powered by advances in artificial intelligence. From foundation models and multimodal learning to biological reasoning and agentic systems, AI has the potential to fundamentally change how we discover, develop, and deliver medicines to patients.  You will help create the scientific foundations behind that future at Pfizer.

We are not looking for one clever model for one clever problem or applying existing models to a single problem. You will develop, extend, and rigorously evaluate advanced AI methods that generate new scientific insights, accelerate experimentation, and enable better decision-making across the drug discovery and development lifecycle. We are building AI that compounds. A method, benchmark or model that works in one disease area should become a foundation that can impact across oncology, immunology/inflammation, internal medicine, vaccines and beyond. You’ll design for that!

Working alongside world-class AI researchers, computational biologists, engineers, and domain experts, you'll tackle some of the most challenging and meaningful problems in healthcare while building technology that has the potential to impact millions of patients worldwide.

Why This Role Is Different
Own Meaningful Scientific Challenges: You will own defined model components, benchmarks, evaluation frameworks, and research workflows that directly influence how AI is applied across Pfizer's R&D organization. You'll build the models, and you'll also decide whether they create real scientific value and whether that value holds up in new contexts.

Where you will push the frontier:  You'll contribute to cutting-edge research across areas such as:

-
- Foundation models and representation learning.
- Multimodal learning across molecular, imaging, clinical and omics data
- Agentic AI and scientific reasoning systems
- Biological Sequence & Structure Modeling
- Graph learning and knowledge graphs
- Clinical & Real-World Data Modeling
- Uncertainty-Aware AI, causal ML and Interpretability

Create Impact Beyond Research Papers
Publishing matters, but the goal is bigger. Your work will help scientists understand disease biology, prioritize experiments, and evaluate therapeutic opportunities across the portfolio. It will speed up medicines for the people waiting on them.

Work at the frontier, with the people who can ship it to patients.

The leader will modernize stewardship across reference data management (RDM), metadata and taxonomy, data quality, hierarchy and mapping management, and market-specific commercial data processes. Scope includes product and market definitions, market hierarchies, brand-indication and brand business unit mappings, activity and account mappings, customer and contract relationships, territory alignment, secondary sales, digital HCP interactions, and other commercially critical reference and mapping domains.

Working closely with Commercial, Legal, and Privacy teams, the role will help ensure that data is used consistently with regulatory requirements

This role will be responsible for establishing multi-functional governance disciplines and codify processes into agentic ways of working:
- Set the agentic stewardship strategy. Define the target-state vision, architecture, operating model and phased roadmap for agentifying U.S. Commercial data stewardship. Automate the high-friction, high-value work first and keep clear human accountability.

À propos de Pratt & Whitney Canada
Pratt & Whitney Canada (P&WC) est un leader mondial de l’innovation aérospatiale, dont le siège social est situé à Longueuil, au Québec, depuis 1928. Nous concevons et fabriquons des moteurs d’aéronefs de nouvelle génération qui propulsent la plus grande flotte mondiale d’avions et d’hélicoptères dans les segments de l’aviation d’affaires, de l’aviation générale et de l’aviation régionale.

Depuis près de 100 ans, nos équipes sont à l’avant-garde des technologies de propulsion, repoussant les limites afin de rendre nos moteurs plus performants et fiables. Nos moteurs soutiennent des missions essentielles, du transport de passagers et de marchandises aux services médicaux d’urgence, aux opérations humanitaires et à la lutte contre les feux de forêt, partout dans le monde.

Un employeur de choix
Pratt & Whitney Canada a été reconnue comme l’un des meilleurs employeurs au Canada en 2026 selon Forbes, et ce, pour une 11e année consécutive. L’entreprise s’est également classée au premier rang des employeurs de l’industrie de l’aérospatiale et de la défense au pays. De plus, notre siège social figure toujours parmi les meilleurs employeurs de la région de Montréal. Ensemble, ces distinctions confirment notre réputation d’employeur de choix à Montréal, au Canada et à l’échelle mondiale.

Pourquoi rejoindre notre équipe?
Pratt & Whitney Canada est à la recherche d’un leader transformationnel pour occuper le poste de Directeur, PMO et excellence opérationnelle. Agissant comme le principal partenaire stratégique du directeur exécutif des technologies numériques, cette personne assurera une maîtrise rigoureuse, une visibilité complète et une exécution disciplinée de l’ensemble du portefeuille de projets numériques de P&WC. Il ne s’agit pas d’un rôle traditionnel de suivi de projets, mais d’un poste de leadership stratégique responsable de l’exécution, de la gouvernance, de la santé financière et de l’amélioration continue d’un portefeuille de transformation numérique de plusieurs millions de dollars.

En supervisant des initiatives complexes dans les domaines de l’ingénierie, de la fabrication, de la chaîne d’approvisionnement, des services après-vente et des fonctions corporatives, le directeur jouera un rôle de liaison essentiel entre P&WC, les organisations de livraison basées en Pologne et le PMO mondial de Pratt & Whitney. En intégrant la responsabilité financière et l’excellence opérationnelle au cadre de gestion du PMO, cette personne veillera à ce que les investissements technologiques stratégiques génèrent une valeur mesurable pour les résultats financiers et une transformation durable de l’entreprise.

Le poste s’effectue à notre établissement de Longueuil , du lundi au vendredi, selon des horaires flexi

- Deep, hands-on expertise in agentic technologies including LLM-based agents, orchestration frameworks such as LangChain or AutoGen, tool integration, context engineering, and retrieval systems with proven experience building these systems at scale

- Strong software and quality engineering foundations with expertise in test architecture, CI/CD pipelines such as Jenkins or GitLab CI, static and dynamic analysis tools, and performance engineering practices
- Proven track record of building and leading engineering teams, including hiring senior talent and successfully driving organizational transformation across multiple teams
- Executive-level communication skills with ability to influence technical and non-technical stakehold

PRIMARY PURPOSE OF THE ROLE:  To direct all aspects associated with global financial statement consolidation process ensuring consolidated and entity statements are stated accurately and in accordance with GAAP, monitoring and maintaining compliance with company policies, procedures and internal controls.

ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES MAY INCLUDE
- Prepares financial statements in accordance with GAAP and all related footnotes.

QUALIFICATIONS

Bachelor's degree with major in accounting from an accredited college or university required.  Master’s degree with major in accounting preferred.  Certified Public Accountant (CPA) designation preferred.

- Pipeline Orchestration: Builds event-driven pipelines and a workflow orchestration platform with robust error handling, logging, and repair, so clinical workflows run reliably at scale. The Jackson Laboratory (JAX) is looking for a Senior Director, Chief Information Security Officer to lead security, technology risk, and security infrastructure across our enterprise and research environments. Reporting to the Chief Information Officer, you will set the enterprise's risk posture alongside business and research leaders, and you will answer for the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the data and systems our scientists depend on.

Protect the science that protects human health.

This is a rare, broad CISO role. Beyond core security, you will own AI security and model risk, identity and access governance, OT/IoT security for lab and research equipment, and independent assurance of our data-privacy program. You will be a trusted partner to researchers and senior leadership, and a regular voice with the executive team.

- Report on risk regularly to enterprise risk teams, senior leaders, and the executive team.

- Energize cross-functional teams, including those you do not directly manage, around shared security outcomes.

Job Family
IT - Development
About Us

At Transamerica, hard work, innovative thinking, and personal accountability are qualities we honor and reward. We understand the potential of leveraging the talents of a diverse workforce. We embrace an environment where employees enjoy a balance between their careers, families, communities, and personal interests.

Ultimately, we appreciate the uniqueness of a company where talented professionals work collaboratively in a positive environment — one focused on helping people look forward and plan for the best life possible while providing tools and solutions that make it easier to get there.

Who We Are

We believe everyone deserves to live their best life. More than a century ago, we were among the first financial services companies in America to serve everyday people from all walks of life .

Today, we’re part of an international holding company, with millions of customers and thousands of employees worldwide. Our insurance, retirement, and investment solutions help people make the most of what’s important to them.

We’re empowered by a vast agent network covering North America, with diversity to match. Together with our nonprofit research institute and foundation, we tune in, step up, and are a force for good — for our customers and the communities where we live, work, and play. United in our purpose, we help people create the financial freedom to live life on their terms.

What We Do

- Establish best practices supporting consistent, scalable manufacturing performance.

A Brief Summary of This Position:
The Director, Enterprise Cybersecurity is responsible for leading and advancing Valmont's global cybersecurity program to protect enterprise information assets, technology platforms, cloud environments, digital solutions, and operational technology systems. Reporting to the Vice President, Cybersecurity & Technology Operations, this role serves as both a strategic cybersecurity leader and a hands-on technical executive, translating enterprise security strategy into operational execution and measurable business outcomes.

The Director provides leadership across security operations, security engineering and architecture, identity and access management, application security, vulnerability management and cyber incident response. The role partners closely with infrastructure, engineering, digital technology, legal, internal audit, and business leaders to ensure security is integrated into enterprise architecture, technology modernization initiatives, and business operations.

This position requires a leader who can effectively balance strategic planning with technical execution, influence executive stakeholders.

Cybersecurity Program Leadership
- Lead execution of Valmont's enterprise cybersecurity strategy, roadmap, and annual priorities.
- Establish and maintain cybersecurity policies, standards, procedures, and operational practices aligned with business and risk management objectives.
- Develop and mature cybersecurity capabilities that support secure business growth, digital transformation, cloud adoption, and operational resilience.
- Promote cybersecurity awareness, accountability, and risk ownership throughout the organization.
- Partner with business and technology leaders to support secure adoption of emerging technologies, AI capabilities, and digital solutions.
- Develop and report cybersecurity KPIs, risk indicators, maturity metrics, and program performance updates to executive leadership.
- Serve as a trusted advisor to leaders regarding cybersecurity risks, emerging threats, and mitigation strategies.
- Drive innovation through automation, orchestration, AI-enabled security operations, and workflow simplification

workday:wolters kluwer:R0059896.description:
Job Posting

About the Role
Millions of professionals rely on Wolters Kluwer to make critical decisions across healthcare, tax, legal, financial services, compliance and corporate performance. As AI reshapes professional work, our customers expect software that is more intelligent, integrated and effective.
Meeting those expectations requires rethinking how products are discovered, built, launched, measured and improved.
This newly created role reflects Wolters Kluwer's commitment to transforming how products are built in the age of AI. Reporting to the Senior Vice President, Product Strategy & Transformation, you will help lead that evolution from the Corporate Strategy Office.
Working in a small enterprise team, you will partner with senior product, engineering, design and business leaders to strengthen the Product System and improve customer value, business outcomes and speed of innovation.
A key focus will be advancing the Agentic Product Development Lifecycle (Agentic PDLC), using AI across product development. You will combine deep product expertise with a hands-on transformation mindset to implement and scale change.

How You Will Work
